_note: Per-deployment data, applied ONCE by the org-roles-backfill-2026-08 runOnce when the content-card org chart becomes rows. Everything here is a DELTA over the cards already in the content document: aim, domain, accountabilities and whyItMatters are carried across from the cards untouched, so a village that edited them keeps its edits. Only structure, naming, seat status and holders are corrected. Source of truth: 'Amora Roles, Notes for Rieki' (Jessica Filkins, 2026-07-30) and the 'From Founder-Held to Sociocracy' transition map inside it.

circles.name: Leadership Circle
circles.purpose: The Core Four. The Visionary Lead plus the three domain leads who each build and hold a circle beneath them.

circles.name: General Coordinating Circle
circles.purpose: Where the circles meet: alignment, budget stewardship, inter-circle coordination, and the decisions no single circle can make alone.

circles.name: Outreach & Growth Circle
circles.purpose: One journey, one circle. Connects with people and guides the whole path in, sales included.

circles.name: Community Circle
circles.purpose: The human experience of the village: events, gathering, care, and the coherence of the team itself.

circles.name: Development Circle
circles.purpose: From drawings to homes: architecture, permitting, construction, infrastructure and the land operations that carry them.

circles.name: Finance & Business Circle
circles.purpose: Fuel for the vision: financial architecture, entity and trust structure, and the businesses the village runs.

circles.name: Advisory Bodies
circles.purpose: Counsel and oversight. Day-to-day work stays in the circles. Approved as represented, with no changes requested.

circles.name: Architecture Circle
circles.purpose: Design of the village's built form, working directly with the Development Lead.

circles.name: Regenerative Agriculture & Permaculture Circle
circles.purpose: Food systems, soil and water, working directly with the Development Lead.

_councilNote: The eight aspirational councils already exist as rows from circles-seed.json. The backfill only moves them to 'forming', because none of them is a working circle yet.
_seatNote: group is the free-text value on the existing card; circleId is where the seat actually belongs. Three card groups matched no circle at all: 'Leadership Circle' (4 cards), 'General Circle' (3 cards, a near-miss on 'General Coordinating Circle') and 'Advisory Bodies' (3 cards), which is 10 of 24 cards pointing at a circle that did not exist in the same document.

seats.name: Business Lead
seats.note: Promoted from Business Development Steward into the Core Four. The transition map puts Ky on Business as the fourth seat, and the notes call it very high priority. Kept as ONE row so the seat's history and holders survive the promotion.
A role today. As the village grows this is the seat most likely to become a circle of its own.
The notes confirm this as the events-focused role and say it is definitely needed, so it reads as an open call and not as forming.
The notes fold this under Community Lead as a sub-circle, and keep it off the Leadership Circle. It carries the independent escalation path for grievances.

seats.name: Potluck Priestess
seats.aim: Hold the village's shared table: the potlucks that keep people eating together.
seats.domain: Potluck rhythm, hosting and the invitations around it.
accountabilities: Calls the potluck and holds its rhythm
seats.whyItMatters: Eating together is the cheapest and most reliable thing a village does to stay one village.

seats.note: Renamed from Rancho Renovation Manager. The notes say it is held by someone who does not live on the land, which is fine this year since nobody will, and they do not name the holder. The override says filled for sixty days and then lapses back to the derived state, so an unnamed holder cannot quietly become permanent.
The notes call Architecture a circle under the Development Lead, not a seat beside one. The seat keeps its row and moves inside the circle that grew from it.
Same as Architecture: a circle under the Development Lead, grown from this seat.
Moves out of the Core Four. Ky covers finance and accounting today; Gate 1 asks for an accountant in seat before October so Ky can move to business development and capital.

_holderNote: Every one of these is a DOCUMENTED holder: a real person in a real seat who may not have an account yet. On their next login the seat-claim card offers the seating to whoever matches the name, and it converts to a member holding with one tap. Nobody is invented here; each name is read from the transition map's 'in seat today' list or the role cards.
